statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail steps to 23% as cash NDX, SMH and NVDA all trade at or within a fraction of their session lows while the 10-year holds a 5.28% session high, yet the move remains an orderly give-back rather than a one-way path.
recommendation: Tail remains inside the watch band at 23%, so the mapped policy state stays WATCH. The afternoon fade flagged in the previous two hours has extended: cash NDX at 30,765.54 now sits just 28.47 points above its 30,737.07 session low, 103.60 points below its own 30,869.14 opening print and 0.81% under the 31,017.53 session high, while SMH prints exactly at its 628.82 session low and NVDA at 234.26 is 0.03 above its own. The long end is the mechanism: the 10-year at 5.28% has fully reversed its post-payrolls drop to 5.16% and sits at the top of today's range. That is a genuine downside-aligned configuration across price, semiconductors, megacap leadership and yields, which is why Tail lifts one point rather than easing. It stays below the block threshold because the decline is a give-back toward value rather than extension away from it, the index is still 0.87% higher on the day, and VIX at 15.68 remains 4.33% lower and well under its 16.24 session high. The published danger window covers 19:00Z to 21:00Z, pairing the Friday power hour and cash close with the weekly futures settlement. Escalation would be a decisive loss of the 30,737.07 cash low with the 10-year above 5.28%; invalidation would be a reclaim of the 30,869.14 opening print. Stress holds 79% on the unresolved yield and energy channels.
headline: Cash NDX 30,765.54 sits 28 points off its session low with SMH exactly at its own and the 10-year at a 5.28% session high, lifting Tail to 23% inside the watch band
body: NQ December futures trade 31,062.00 (+301.50, +0.98%) on a quote timed 17:16:21Z, inside a 30,760.25-31,282.25 session range from a 30,771.25 open on about 461.5k contracts, with a 31,056.25/31,056.50 bid/ask. The defining development of this hour is that the retracement first flagged at 15:37Z has not merely held, it has extended, and it has done so with cross-sectional alignment that was absent an hour ago. Cash NDX is 30,765.54 (+263.98, +0.87%) on a 17:26:23Z quote against a 30,869.14 open, a 30,737.07 session low and a 31,017.53 session high: the index is 28.47 points above its low, 103.60 points below its own opening print and 252.0 points, 0.81%, under the high. Semiconductor and megacap leadership has gone with it rather than diverging from it. SMH is 628.82 (+11.01, +1.78%) at 17:27:04Z and that figure is exactly the bottom of its 628.82-636.25 session range, so the basket prints at its session low. NVDA is 234.26 (+3.40, +1.47%) at 17:27:22Z against a 234.23 session low and the 237.87 intraday record it set earlier today, leaving it three cents off its low and 3.61 under its record. The long end is the transmission mechanism and it is confirmed: the CBOE 10-year yield index is 5.28 (+0.04, +0.76%) at 17:11:35Z at the very top of a 5.16-5.28 range, having fully reversed the post-payrolls drop to 5.16%, with the Federal Reserve H.15 release carrying 5.29% for the 10-year and 4.88% for the 2-year as of 30 September. Reporting corroborates the mechanism directly: yields fell immediately after the employment report and then rebounded, pushing equities off their session highs. Four independent amplifiers therefore point the same way at the same time, price near a session extreme, semiconductors at a session low, megacap leadership at a session low and the long end at a session high, which is why Tail steps up one point to 23% rather than easing toward the 20% floor it held overnight. It stays inside the watch band and below the 25% block threshold for three concrete reasons. First, the direction of travel is toward value rather than away from it: this is the surrender of an opening gain back through the opening print, which is mean reversion operating, not mean reversion failing, and the index remains 0.87% higher on the day. Second, the magnitude is small for a record-area tape, 0.90% from high to low in the cash index. Third, volatility is actively declining: VIX is 15.68 (-0.71, -4.33%) at 17:11:01Z against a 16.39 previous close and a 16.24 session high, an absolute level and a direction both inconsistent with violent directional repricing. The driver of the whole session is verified at the primary source. The Bureau of Labor Statistics Employment Situation Summary, released 08:30 ET today, reported September nonfarm payrolls of +29,000 against a 90,000 consensus, unemployment at 4.2%, and average hourly earnings up five cents, 0.1%, to $37.81 and 3.0% over twelve months. That miss cut October rate-hike expectations sharply and is the mechanism behind a 1%-plus intraday index advance that has now been given back. Energy remains the most volatile macro channel: WTI is 91.48 (-1.39, -1.50%) at 17:17:09Z from a 93.46 open inside an 88.11-93.51 range, a 5.40 intraday span, after the G7 agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel reserves over four months including a substantial diesel tranche within the first twenty days, with diesel reported near $6.37 a gallon. The combination of a soft labour print, an unresolved inflation channel, a long end back at multi-decade high territory and an unsettled energy complex supports Stress at 79% in the high band while Tail stays at 23%. Confidence is 89%: this assessment holds current verified quotes for NQ, NDX, VIX, the 10-year index, WTI, SMH and NVDA, all timed between 17:11Z and 17:27Z, together with the primary payrolls release, the H.15 yield file, the verified seven-day U.S. calendar and two verified published news items. The shared Finviz context file was read and rejected for material use: its most recent collection is dated 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z with a partial status and both its futures and calendar sections unavailable, far outside the 90-minute freshness limit, so this assessment rests entirely on independent current research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published Claude hours are available, covering the 17:00Z hour on 1 October through the 16:00Z hour today. Tail ran from 20% to 27% across the window. It opened at 20% and held that watch floor for fourteen consecutive hours, through the U.S. afternoon on 1 October and the entire Asian session, then stepped to 21% at 07:00Z, 23% at 08:00Z and 22% at 09:00Z as the European-morning advance gained directional efficiency. It returned to 20% for the 10:00Z and 11:00Z hours, then climbed through the payrolls release to 24% at 12:00Z, 25% at 13:00Z and a window peak of 27% at 14:00Z. Those two hours, 13:00Z and 14:00Z, are the only ones in the window published in the block band, and they were published when NQ held within 0.10% of its session extreme with no meaningful pullback. Tail mapped back to 22% for both the 15:00Z and 16:00Z hours once a 0.81% retracement was actually observed and then held. Stress stayed in the high band throughout, between 74% and 79%, and Confidence held 88-89%. Dominant mode was mixed for twenty of the twenty-four hours, with trend-up recorded only for the 08:00Z and 09:00Z European-morning hours and the 12:00Z to 14:00Z post-payrolls stretch.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail at 23% for the current 17:00Z hour and the 18:00Z hour, matching the observed downside alignment, then lifts to 24% for 19:00Z and 20:00Z. That pair is the published danger window, extended to 21:00Z to capture the weekly futures settlement: it places the Friday power hour and the cash close against a record-area level that has already failed once today, with the long end at a session high and liquidity thinning. No slot is published in the block band, because the amplifier stack is currently expressing as an orderly give-back toward the opening print rather than as extension away from it, and because VIX is falling rather than rising. The escalation condition on the danger-window hours is a decisive loss of the 30,737.07 cash session low together with the 10-year holding above 5.28%; the invalidation is a reclaim of the 30,869.14 opening print or an orderly close inside today's 30,737.07-31,017.53 cash range. Tail eases to 21% at 21:00Z, when CME equity index futures settle for the week and only the first minutes of the hour remain tradable. Those futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday 4 October, so the final nineteen slots sit entirely inside a market closure and carry a flat 20% watch floor rather than a projected curve. A closed market offers no price path to deny, while mapping an unresolved record-area weekly close into the lowest band would misrepresent it as benign. Stress steps from 79% to 78% at 21:00Z and to 77% from 07:00Z on Saturday on the explicit assumption that no fresh weekend escalation emerges, and Confidence decays from 89% to 72% across the closed stretch because ageing evidence degrades certainty about the state rather than the state itself. The first live catalyst is Monday's 14:00Z ISM Services PMI; Wednesday's 18:00Z FOMC minutes remain the most credible delayed-second-leg mechanism for the long end; September CPI is verified for 14 October and therefore sits outside this window.
